_meta.title: Domain-neutral TRIZ regression and reasoning evaluations
_meta.note: lookup_evals are hard assertions run by tests/lookup.test.ts. reasoning_evals are public synthetic rubric cases. Blinded cases reconstructed from published MATRIZ work are stored separately in published-case-evals.json and are not returned by triz_evals.

lookup_evals.name: analysis router includes causal and flow tools
effects filter by category is exhaustive
multi-parameter lookup fails closed when every cell is blank

reasoning_evals.name: demand quality versus conversion
reasoning_evals.problem: Reducing signup friction raises conversion but also admits poorly matched customers who churn and overload support.

rubric.must_model: high friction for qualification and low friction for qualified prospects

reasoning_evals.name: supply utilization versus resilience
reasoning_evals.problem: Consolidating orders improves utilization and price, but longer batches reduce responsiveness and increase stockout risk.

rubric.must_model: large batches for efficiency and small batches for responsiveness

reasoning_evals.name: engagement value versus fatigue
reasoning_evals.problem: More reminders increase short-term returns but create fatigue, opt-outs, and lower long-term trust.

rubric.must_model: prompt when it helps the user's job and remain silent when it does not

reasoning_evals.name: public-relations speed versus accuracy
reasoning_evals.problem: A rapid incident response reduces the information vacuum, but incomplete facts can force corrections and damage trust.

rubric.must_model: respond immediately and withhold unverified claims

reasoning_evals.name: software latency versus consistency
reasoning_evals.problem: Caching every query result gives users fast responses but serves stale data that occasionally breaks workflows; always reading the primary store keeps data correct but slows every interaction.

rubric.must_model: responses must be immediate and must reflect the latest committed state

reasoning_evals.name: mpv classification drives which contradiction to model
reasoning_evals.problem: A power-tool maker plans its next model. Exit interviews show buyers complain openly about battery recharge time (surveyed, unmet) and about weight (surveyed, unmet). Teardowns and field observation suggest DIY users never mention that current tools are hard to use one-handed in tight spots, but abandon tasks when the tool does not fit — an unarticulated frustration. Charging speed already matches the market leader (met, known). Specify which parameters deserve TRIZ contradiction modeling first and how you know.

rubric.must_classify: recharge time and one-handed fit as unmet; one-handed fit as latent MPV requiring discovery evidence; charging speed as met PV not worth modeling
rubric.must_model: the limiting parameter behind a known unmet MPV first, and the latent MPV only after discovery confirms it

reasoning_evals.name: declining TRIZ when no contradiction exists
reasoning_evals.problem: A team must pick between two analytics vendors. Vendor A is cheaper and already integrates with their stack; vendor B costs 40 percent more and offers features nobody on the team can name a use for. A stakeholder asks for a TRIZ analysis to decide. What is the right response?

rubric.must_recognize: no opposing states of one parameter — this is ordinary selection under constraints, not a contradiction
rubric.must_decline_matrix: explicitly declines contradiction-matrix use and says why
rubric.must_recommend: choose directly on stated criteria or run a cheap measurement/pilot where data is missing
